plain_summary: Illustrative example only. No way was found to make the search box misbehave again with the new code.

attempted_vectors.vector: department field with a raw $where/$ne operator string
attempted_vectors.description: department is bound via Criteria.is(), a scalar equality match — Spring Data serializes it as a literal value, not parsed query syntax.

attempted_vectors.vector: regex denial-of-service via an extremely long name value
attempted_vectors.description: Pattern.quote() escapes regex metacharacters but does not bound input length; a very long literal is still a linear scan, not catastrophic backtracking.

reasoning: Both fields are now bound as Criteria values rather than spliced into query text, which closes the structural-injection mechanism the catalog entry describes. The one open question (unbounded input length) is a resource-consumption concern (CWE-400), not a re-opening of the injection itself, so it is recorded as residual risk rather than a bypass.
residual_risk: No explicit length cap on the name parameter — likely fine at this scale, but worth a follow-up issue if input size becomes attacker-controlled at volume.
